title: API Data Fetching
description: Build a frontend that interacts with a REST API. Tests asynchronous JavaScript, React state management, error handling, and performance optimization.

seo.overviewTitle: Robust API Data Fetching, Caching & Error Handling
seo.overviewBody: Production web applications must handle asynchronous data loading gracefully. Employers look for developers who manage loading states, race conditions, stale-while-revalidate caching, automatic retries, and user-friendly error boundaries without crashing the user interface.

deliverables.title: 1. Data Fetching & Caching Strategy Doc
deliverables.desc: Architectural breakdown comparing custom fetch hooks vs TanStack Query (React Query) and SWR caching mechanisms.

deliverables.title: 2. Custom Hook & Data Fetching Module
deliverables.desc: TypeScript custom hook featuring loading indicators, refetching on window focus, optimistic updates, and exponential backoff.

deliverables.title: 3. Error Boundary & Skeleton UI Demo
deliverables.desc: Skeleton loader component and React Error Boundary wrapping the data grid during network failures or API rate limiting.

faqs.question: What is Stale-While-Revalidate (SWR) caching?
faqs.answer: SWR is a HTTP cache invalidation strategy where the client first returns cached (stale) data immediately, then dispatches a fetch request (revalidates) in the background to update the cache.

faqs.question: How do you prevent race conditions during fast search inputs?
faqs.answer: Race conditions occur when an earlier API request resolves after a later request. You prevent this using AbortController signals to cancel pending fetch calls when query state changes, or debouncing input handlers.

faqs.question: Why use TanStack Query instead of plain useEffect + fetch?
faqs.answer: Plain useEffect fetches lack built-in request deduplication, cache sharing across components, automatic background revalidation, retry mechanisms, and pagination state management.
